Misconfigurations.Title: Load balancers should drop invalid headers
Misconfigurations.Description:
Passing unknown or invalid headers through to the target poses a potential risk of compromise.
By setting drop_invalid_header_fields to true, anything that does not conform to well known, defined headers will be removed by the load balancer.
Misconfigurations.Message: Application load balancer is not set to drop invalid headers.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set drop_invalid_header_fields to true

Misconfigurations.Title: Use of plain HTTP.
Misconfigurations.Description:
Plain HTTP is unencrypted and human-readable. This means that if a malicious actor was to eavesdrop on your connection, they would be able to see all of your data flowing back and forth.
You should use HTTPS, which is HTTP over an encrypted (TLS) connection, meaning eavesdroppers cannot read your traffic.
Misconfigurations.Message: Listener for application load balancer does not use HTTPS.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Switch to HTTPS to benefit from TLS security features

Misconfigurations.Title: No unauthorized access to API Gateway methods
Misconfigurations.Description: API Gateway methods should generally be protected by authorization or api key. OPTION verb calls can be used without authorization
Misconfigurations.Message: Authorization is not enabled for this method.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use and authorization method or require API Key

Misconfigurations.Title: CloudWatch log groups should be encrypted using CMK
Misconfigurations.Description: CloudWatch log groups are encrypted by default, however, to get the full benefit of controlling key rotation and other KMS aspects a KMS CMK should be used.
Misconfigurations.Message: Log group is not encrypted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable CMK encryption of CloudWatch Log Groups

Misconfigurations.Title: Ensure that response caching is enabled for your Amazon API Gateway REST APIs.
Misconfigurations.Description: A REST API in API Gateway is a collection of resources and methods that are integrated with backend HTTP endpoints, Lambda functions, or other AWS services. You can enable API caching in Amazon API Gateway to cache your endpoint responses. With caching, you can reduce the number of calls made to your endpoint and also improve the latency of requests to your API.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cache data is not enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable cache

Misconfigurations.Title: aws_instance should activate session tokens for Instance Metadata Service.
Misconfigurations.Description: IMDS v2 (Instance Metadata Service) introduced session authentication tokens which improve security when talking to IMDS. By default aws_instance resource sets IMDS session auth tokens to be optional. To fully protect IMDS you need to enable session tokens by using metadata_options block and its http_tokens variable set to required.
Misconfigurations.Message: Instance does not require IMDS access to require a token.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable HTTP token requirement for IMDS

Misconfigurations.Title: A security group rule should not allow unrestricted egress to any IP address.
Misconfigurations.Description: Opening up ports to connect out to the public internet is generally to be avoided. You should restrict access to IP addresses or ranges that are explicitly required where possible.
Misconfigurations.Message: Security group rule allows unrestricted egress to any IP address.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Set a more restrictive cidr range

Misconfigurations.Title: Missing description for security group rule.
Misconfigurations.Description:
Security group rules should include a description for auditing purposes.

Simplifies auditing, debugging, and managing security groups.
Misconfigurations.Message: Security group rule does not have a description.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add descriptions for all security groups rules

Misconfigurations.Title: Instance with unencrypted block device.
Misconfigurations.Description: Block devices should be encrypted to ensure sensitive data is held securely at rest.
Misconfigurations.Message: Root block device is not encrypted.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Turn on encryption for all block devices

Misconfigurations.Title: Point in time recovery should be enabled to protect DynamoDB table
Misconfigurations.Description:
DynamoDB tables should be protected against accidentally or malicious write/delete actions by ensuring that there is adequate protection.
By enabling point-in-time-recovery you can restore to a known point in the event of loss of data.
Misconfigurations.Message: Point-in-time recovery is not enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable point in time recovery

Misconfigurations.Title: DynamoDB tables should use at rest encryption with a Customer Managed Key
Misconfigurations.Description: Using AWS managed keys does not allow for fine grained control. DynamoDB tables are encrypted by default using AWS managed encryption keys. To increase control of the encryption and control the management of factors like key rotation, use a Customer Managed Key.
Misconfigurations.Message: Table encryption explicitly uses the default KMS key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable server side encryption with a customer managed key

Misconfigurations.Title: ECR Repository should use customer managed keys to allow more control
Misconfigurations.Description: Images in the ECR repository are encrypted by default using AWS managed encryption keys. To increase control of the encryption and control the management of factors like key rotation, use a Customer Managed Key.
Misconfigurations.Message: Repository is not encrypted using KMS.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use customer managed keys

Misconfigurations.Title: EKS Clusters should have cluster control plane logging turned on
Misconfigurations.Description: By default cluster control plane logging is not turned on. Logging is available for audit, api, authenticator, controllerManager and scheduler. All logging should be turned on for cluster control plane.
Misconfigurations.Message: Control plane controller manager logging is not enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for the EKS control plane

Misconfigurations.Title: EKS Clusters should have cluster control plane logging turned on
Misconfigurations.Description: By default cluster control plane logging is not turned on. Logging is available for audit, api, authenticator, controllerManager and scheduler. All logging should be turned on for cluster control plane.
Misconfigurations.Message: Control plane scheduler logging is not enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable logging for the EKS control plane

Misconfigurations.Title: EKS should have the encryption of secrets enabled
Misconfigurations.Description: EKS cluster resources should have the encryption_config block set with protection of the secrets resource.
Misconfigurations.Message: Cluster does not have secret encryption enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable encryption of EKS secrets

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 Bucket Logging
Misconfigurations.Description: Ensures S3 bucket logging is enabled for S3 buckets
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket has logging disabled
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Add a logging block to the resource to enable access logging

Misconfigurations.Title: S3 encryption should use Customer Managed Keys
Misconfigurations.Description:
Encryption using AWS keys provides protection for your S3 buckets. To gain greater control over encryption, such as key rotation, access policies, and auditability, use customer managed keys (CMKs) with SSE-KMS.
Note that SSE-KMS is not supported for S3 server access logging destination buckets; in such cases, use SSE-S3 instead.
Misconfigurations.Message: Bucket does not encrypt data with a customer managed key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use SSE-KMS with a customer managed key (CMK)

Misconfigurations.Title: Secrets Manager should use customer managed keys
Misconfigurations.Description: Secrets Manager encrypts secrets by default using a default key created by AWS. To ensure control and granularity of secret encryption, CMK's should be used explicitly.
Misconfigurations.Message: Secret explicitly uses the default key.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Use customer managed keys

Misconfigurations.Title: VPC Flow Logs is a feature that enables you to capture information about the IP traffic going to and from network interfaces in your VPC. After you've created a flow log, you can view and retrieve its data in Amazon CloudWatch Logs. It is recommended that VPC Flow Logs be enabled for packet "Rejects" for VPCs.
Misconfigurations.Description: VPC Flow Logs provide visibility into network traffic that traverses the VPC and can be used to detect anomalous traffic or insight during security workflows.
Misconfigurations.Message: VPC does not have VPC Flow Logs enabled.
Misconfigurations.Resolution: Enable flow logs for VPC
